problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function on ℝᵈ with globally L-Lipschitz gradient, L > 0. A global lower bound b satisfies f(x₀) − b ≤ Δ. The starting point x₀ and gap bound Δ ≥ 0 are public, while b and f are hidden.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CorruptedFirstOrderNonconvex.lean — Space, Params, spec.Public, spec.Instance, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: One query at x returns a pair (v,u). On a clean call, |v − f(x)| ≤ ε²/(128L). Clean values at repeated queries to x may differ.

oracle.label: inexact_gradient
oracle.details: The same call returns a vector u. On every clean call at x, u equals the same hidden g(x), with ‖g(x) − ∇f(x)‖ ≤ ε/8.

distinctive_assumptions.label: biased_oracle
distinctive_assumptions.details: The hidden field g may have a persistent additive error. Repeating a clean query returns exactly the same gradient vector, and neither clean reply component has a centering assumption.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain, gradient vectors and output all use the Euclidean norm on ℝᵈ, with public d ∈ ℕ.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Every reachable query history has at most k replies violating either clean condition. A reply violating both counts once. Corruption locations may depend on the history, and corruption magnitudes are unrestricted. The algorithm knows k, d, L, Δ, ε, x₀ and the failure tolerance. It receives no flag identifying corrupted calls.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CorruptedFirstOrderNonconvex.lean — Params, Reachable, errors, accurate, spec.publicInput, spec.Reply, spec.admissible. LongTails/Template.lean — Oracle.answer

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return one point x satisfying ‖∇f(x)‖ ≤ ε for public ε > 0. The criterion uses the true gradient at the returned point.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: The probability that the returned point violates the gradient-norm bound is at most the public failure tolerance δ ∈ [0,1/4], under the product law of the algorithm seed and the oracle seed sequence. The endpoint δ = 0 requires almost-sure success.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The oracle combines inexact function values and a repeatable biased gradient field with a single pathwise budget for arbitrarily corrupted joint replies.

descriptionHtml:
Nonconvex Stationarity with Corrupted First-Order Queries

We seek an approximate stationary point of a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rd→R in Euclidean dimension d. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz for L>0, and its value at a given starting point lies within Δ≥0 of a global lower bound. For a tolerance ε>0, the oracle returns an approximate function value and a fixed gradient approximation at the query point, except on at most k calls in any possible history, where k is a nonnegative integer. The goal is an output x¯∈Rd satisfying ∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε with failure probability at most δ∈[0,1/4].

The underlying optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x). We use the Euclidean norm ∥⋅∥. The algorithm receives the dimension d∈{0,1,…}, the starting point x0∈Rd, and the parameters L,Δ,ε,k,δ.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere and satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈Rd.

Assumption 2 (Initial objective gap). There exists ℓ∈R such that ℓ≤f(x)for every x∈Rd,f(x0)−ℓ≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Corrupted first-order replies). There exists a fixed map g:Rd→Rd satisfying ∥g(x)−∇f(x)∥≤ε/8,x∈Rd. At any query point x∈Rd, the oracle returns a pair (v,u)∈R×Rd. A reply is accurate when both conditions hold: |v−f(x)|≤ε2128L,u=g(x). Every finite history obtainable from any sequence of queries and any choices of oracle randomness contains at most k inaccurate replies. These replies may be arbitrary.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy P(∥∇f(x¯)∥>ε)≤δ, where P is the joint law of the algorithm and oracle randomness, which are independent of one another.

theorems.formulaHtml: ⌈16⋅L⋅Δε2⌉++5⋅k+4

comparisonHtml:
Let f:Rd→R have L-Lipschitz gradient and f(x0)−inff≤Δ, with L,ε>0 and Δ≥0. A clean reply at x gives a value within ε2/(128L) of f(x) and a fixed vector g(x) satisfying ∥g(x)−∇f(x)∥≤ε/8. On every reachable history, at most k replies may be replaced adaptively by arbitrary pairs. The target is Pr(∥∇f(xout)∥>ε)≤δ for 0≤δ≤1/4.

Sufficient oracle budgets for nonconvex stationarity under adaptive corruption.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) CorruptedFirstOrderDescent (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(1+k+LΔ/ε2) joint value–gradient calls
(2) Derived bound: majority-vote gradient descent (Nesterov 2018, sec. 1.2.3) O((k+1)(1+LΔ/ε2)) gradient calls, including 2k+1 per vote (1): Additive dependence on k saves a factor of order min{k+1,T} for k,T≥1. At k≍T≥1, O(T2) falls to O(T). Rates match at k=0. (1) needs accurate function values in addition to gradients.
(3) Stochastic line search (Scheinberg and Xie 2025, Thm. 6, corrupted value oracle) High-probability hitting time above the oracle noise floor. Each trial uses one gradient and two value calls. Rates are incomparable across fault models. (1) returns an ε-stationary point for every admissible fault pattern. (3) bounds the time to visit one under probabilistic faults with bounded value errors. (1) needs a known fault cap k and repeatable clean gradients. (3) allows stochastic gradients without a fault cap.

Abbr: T=LΔ/ε2.

Nesterov, Yurii. 2018. Lectures on Convex Optimization. 2nd ed. Vol. 137. Springer Optimization and Its Applications. Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-91578-4.
Scheinberg, Katya, and Miaolan Xie. 2025. Stochastic Adaptive Optimization with Unreliable Inputs: A Unified Framework for High-Probability Complexity Analysis. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2511.19411.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2

open MeasureTheory OracleTemplate
open scoped ENNReal

namespace LongTails.Setups.CorruptedFirstOrderNonconvex

abbrev Space (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  L : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  k : ℕ
  failure : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ≥0∞) (1 / 4)
  x0 : Space d

inductive Reachable {X Y : Type} (O : Oracle X Y) : List ((Fin 1 × X) × Y) → Prop
  | nil : Reachable O []
  | snoc {h} (hh : Reachable O h) (q : Fin 1 × X) (s : O.Seed h.length) :
      Reachable O (h ++ [(q, O.answer h q s)])

noncomputable def errors {X : Type} (clean : X → ℝ × X → Prop)
    (h : List ((Fin 1 × X) × (ℝ × X))) : ℕ := by
  classical exact (h.filter fun e => ¬clean e.1.2 e.2).length

def accurate (p : Params) (f : Space p.d → ℝ) (g : Space p.d → Space p.d)
    (x : Space p.d) (r : ℝ × Space p.d) : Prop :=
  |r.1 - f x| ≤ p.ε ^ 2 / (128 * p.L) ∧ r.2 = g x

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Space p.d → ℝ
  Query p := Space p.d
  Reply p := ℝ × Space p.d
  Output p := Space p.d
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.L ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ lower : ℝ, (∀ x, lower ≤ f x) ∧ f p.x0 - lower ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    ∃ g : Space p.d → Space p.d, (∀ x, ‖g x - gradient f x‖ ≤ p.ε / 8) ∧
      ∀ h, Reachable O h → errors (accurate p f g) h ≤ p.k
  successful p f out P := (P : Measure _) {s | p.ε < ‖gradient f (out s)‖} ≤ p.failure.val

end LongTails.Setups.CorruptedFirstOrderNonconvex
